summary: Clarify the actual command boundary: standalone VM.log list is read-only for logging configuration, output=... configures even when combined with list, rotation has global scope, and JDK 25 presence-dispatched action options must be omitted rather than serialized as false.

criteria: Read-only inspection must preserve logging configuration even when helpers compose arguments.
Per-output authorization and retention must not be silently expanded by a VM-wide action.
Version-sensitive diagnostic parser behavior must use primary implementation and matching runtime evidence.
Continue distinguishing syntax/source explanation, application coverage and cost/retention claims.
Preserve the existing strong selection, runtime-field scope, async and lifecycle constraints.

baseline.authorship: Package was clean at assignment. The final four-file owned diff is this reviewer's work; no prior uncommitted changes were present.

findingsCorrected.finding: The pre-existing statement that help/list inspection does not change logging configuration lacked the standalone-command boundary.
findingsCorrected.evidence: jdk-25-ga LogDiagnosticCommand::execute applies output/what/decorators configuration before executing list. Temurin 25.0.3+9 confirmed output=file=a.log list changes gc-only/time decorators to all=info/default uptime decorators while returning the requested listing successfully.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A helper that adds output=... as an apparent listing filter can broaden logging and change formatting during an inspection-only task.
findingsCorrected.fix: Clarify standalone read-only commands, treat output as configuration, and filter captured listing text locally.

findingsCorrected.finding: The rotation guidance did not explicitly connect output=... to the VM-wide rotation action.
findingsCorrected.evidence: JDK 25 jcmd documentation specifies global rotation; LogDiagnosticCommand calls LogConfiguration::rotate_all_outputs(). An isolated two-file test with an output selector still produced both a.log.0 and b.log.0 containing their respective expected tags.
findingsCorrected.consequence: An attempted one-file rotation can consume another output's retention slots; adding output can also reconfigure that file.
findingsCorrected.fix: State global eligible-output scope and explain that this command cannot satisfy a one-output-only mutation contract.

findingsCorrected.finding: Generated command builders may assume false-valued action fields disable those actions.
findingsCorrected.evidence: jdk-25-ga checks option presence for disable and rotate. Temurin 25.0.3+9 tests showed rotate=false archives both files and disable=false removes file outputs and changes stdout/stderr to all=off.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A serialized default false option can rotate or disable logging unintentionally.
findingsCorrected.fix: Omit unused action options and pin these parser semantics to the target build rather than generalizing across runtimes.

observedResults: Standalone list preserved all four output configurations and did not rotate files.
list with output=file=a.log changed a.log from all=off,gc=info with time decorators to all=info with uptime decorators; b.log configuration remained unchanged.
rotate with output=file=a.log and explicit preserved settings still created nonempty archives for a.log and b.log.
rotate=false also archived both file outputs.
disable=false removed both file outputs and changed standard outputs to all=off.

failuresAndLimits.observed: Initial standalone-list control passed. The output-plus-list case successfully demonstrated configuration broadening, then the isolated JVM crashed in DestroyJavaVM during shutdown while broad logging remained enabled. EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION; target exit 1.
failuresAndLimits.resolution: Preserved the failure. Subsequent probes restore only the deliberately changed owned output before shutdown, after recording and asserting the semantic result.
failuresAndLimits.limit: Root cause was not established, and no universal crash claim was added to the skill. The clean final run does not prove broad-logging shutdown is safe.

failuresAndLimits.observed: Configuration comparison retained the informational '(reconfigured)' marker because its normalization regex was over-escaped. Actual levels/decorators were unchanged in the rotate-with-output case; its target exited 0.
failuresAndLimits.resolution: A separate final script uses exact string removal of that marker for semantic comparison. Raw outputs remain intact and archives/content checks were retained. The five-condition final run passed.

assumptionsAndLimitations: The skill remains a logging evidence-production skill; no subsystem diagnosis or application implementation was added.
Standalone read-only means logging configuration is not changed. This is not a zero-overhead or no-attach-side-effects claim.
Version-sensitive presence-dispatched actions are explicitly tied to jdk-25-ga source and observed Temurin 25.0.3+9; other builds require their own evidence.
The global rotation test used two distinct rotating file outputs with filecount=2 and filesize=0. It does not claim all destinations support rotation.
The isolated shutdown crash is preserved and unroot-caused; no fix to the JVM or broad production reliability claim is implied.
Development cases are intentionally small and differ by only one argument. Their PowerShell syntax and inputs are validated; independent agent effectiveness is not measured.
All required repository-wide checks remain delegated to the coordinator.
